etymology.root: French terroir, from Latin territorium; older French sense 'soil, ground'

text.what: The claim that a wine tastes of where it grew — soil, slope, aspect, weather, and the habits of the people farming it. In France it is also a legal argument, because appellations are drawn on it.

kin.as: The unit Burgundy uses to make the claim specific.
The variety most often held up as the transmitter, whether or not it is.
